air-work to air, REQUEST re 5cdc74 (DEF-4012), one choice the assign does not settle; both reviews name it (REQUEST CHANGES both; everything else is a fix batch of mine).

The problem in plain words: under design (b), a nested checkout's own HEAD vouches for its files. So a checkout that APPEARS during a call vouches for itself: a fresh `git clone` into models/, `cp -r ../lib models/lib` carrying its .git (the "copy" slip the module exists for), `git submodule update --init`, `git worktree add models/wt`. All reported before this lane; all silent now, except their `.git` pointer file, which still reports alone.

A (my recommendation): ask a nested git only for a checkout the previous check already knew (its HEAD stored in the baseline). A new checkout reports its files once, as on main, and every later pull is silent. It also covers a junk .git and a repo planted and committed in one call. Cost: `submodule update --init` and `worktree add` under a protected path report once per new checkout (as today), and the pointer file goes with them, consistent. Needs the stored heads refreshed on a call that moves no file (git init + commit), about 2 ms per 1,000 files on the peek.

B: any checkout found is asked (as committed). New clones, copies and submodule inits are silent; the pointer file then needs its own rule (account it when its directory is a checkout with a readable HEAD).

Smaller, same area, my default unless you say otherwise: a commit inside a gitignored nested clone in the same call (`fix && git -C models/clone commit`) is silent under A and B alike, and no PR or CI ever sees it; I document it as a limit in docs/HOOKS.md (which I add to my claim with its assets twin) rather than build an @{upstream} rule nobody measured.
